evals.name: product-launch-meeting
evals.prompt:
Format these meeting notes:

Date: May 15
Attendees: product, eng, marketing
We discussed the upcoming v2 launch. Marketing wants to push the date to June 1 so they can run a campaign. Eng says the backend is ready but the mobile app needs another week for QA. We agreed to soft-launch the web version on May 22 and hold the full launch including mobile until June 1. Action items: Sarah to draft the campaign brief by Friday, Tom to confirm QA timeline with the mobile team, Lisa to update the roadmap.
evals.expected_output: A formatted_notes.md with title, one-sentence summary, and 3-5 key points extracted from the meeting notes

assertions.description: formatted_notes.md exists in the output directory

assertions.description: The file contains a ## Summary section

assertions.name: has-key-points-section
assertions.description: The file contains a ## Key Points section

assertions.name: summary-is-one-sentence
assertions.description: The summary is exactly one sentence (ends with a single period, not multiple sentences)

assertions.name: key-points-are-distilled
assertions.description: Key points are distilled from the notes, not copied verbatim — they capture decisions and actions in the agent's own words

evals.name: api-rate-limiting-research
evals.prompt:
Format these research notes:

Topic: API rate limiting strategies
Looked into token bucket vs leaky bucket. Token bucket allows bursting up to a max capacity, good for APIs where occasional spikes are acceptable. Leaky bucket smooths traffic into a constant output rate, better for downstream systems that can't handle bursts. Fixed window counting is simplest to implement but has boundary spike problem — requests cluster at window edges. Sliding window log is most accurate but memory-intensive. Redis sorted sets work well for sliding window. Most production APIs use token bucket because it balances fairness and burst tolerance. Need to also consider per-user vs per-IP vs per-API-key granularity.
evals.expected_output: A formatted_notes.md with title, one-sentence summary, and 3-5 key points about API rate limiting strategies
